title: GUSTA-EVO: A prospective study of taste dysfunction and its relationship to peripheral neurotoxicity during enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab for urothelial carcinoma
summary:
Patients with bladder cancer and other cancers of the urinary tract are increasingly treated with a combination of two medications, enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab. This treatment can cause various side effects, including changes in taste and nerve damage, which may lead to symptoms such as tingling or numbness in the hands and feet.

Changes in taste can reduce the enjoyment of food, decrease food intake, and negatively affect nutritional status and quality of life. However, it is not yet well understood how taste changes develop during treatment, how severe they become, whether they improve over time, or whether they are associated with nerve damage.

The aim of this study is to systematically investigate changes in taste during treatment and to examine their relationship with nerve damage, nutritional status, and quality of life.

The study includes adult patients who are already receiving treatment with enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab for their cancer.

Taste function will be assessed before treatment, at predefined time points during treatment, and at the end of treatment using special taste test strips. In addition, nutritional status, patient-perceived taste changes, and symptoms of nerve damage will be evaluated using questionnaires and examinations of nerve function.

The findings are expected to improve our understanding of treatment-related taste disturbances and their possible association with nerve damage. This knowledge may help improve supportive care for affected patients in the future.

This is an observational study. Participation will not change the patients' cancer treatment. All assessments will be performed during already scheduled study visits, without requiring additional hospital visits.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥18 years at the time of signing the written informed consent form.

2. Enrollment in either of the prospective observational studies P-EVOLVE or P-EVOLUTION.

3. Histologically confirmed urothelial carcinoma in one of the following clinical settings:
   - Muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma with planned perioperative treatment with enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab within P-EVOLVE.
   - Locally advanced, unresectable or metastatic urothelial carcinoma with planned first-line treatment with enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab within P-EVOLUTION.

4. Eligibility to receive enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab according to the respective prescribing information.

5. Predominantly oral nutritional intake.

6. Ability to undergo standardized objective taste testing using taste strips.

7. Written informed consent for participation in the GUSTA-EVO substudy before any substudy-specific assessments.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Contraindications to enfortumab vedotin and/or pembrolizumab according to the respective prescribing information.

2. Prior systemic treatment for muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma in patients enrolled in the P-EVOLVE cohort.

3. Prior systemic treatment for locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma in patients enrolled in the P-EVOLUTION cohort.

4. Previous treatment with enfortumab vedotin, other monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE)-based antibody-drug conjugates, or PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors.

5. Neoadjuvant or adjuvant platinum-based chemotherapy within the preceding 12 months in patients enrolled in the P-EVOLUTION cohort.

6. Inability to undergo standardized objective taste testing or absence of predominantly oral nutritional intake.

7. Absence of written informed consent for participation in the GUSTA-EVO substudy.
